scope.quote: We examine the relation between proximity to debt covenant violation and the following three measures of earnings management: accounting earnings management, real earnings management, and total earnings management.

scope.quote: We examine the relation between proximity to debt covenant violation and the following three measures of earnings management: accounting earnings management, real earnings management, and total earnings management.
Our results indicate that firms close to violation or in technical default of debt covenants engage in higher levels of TEM compared to firms far from violation.
Equation (7) is our starting point and focuses on the debt covenant incentive to manage earnings
Our study differs from Kim et al. (2011) in several aspects. First, we examine total earnings management (TEM) as well as both AEM and REM.
EM in Eq. (7) is either AEM or REM or TEM.

review_notes: Scope: select Equation (7) / Table 2 Panels A–C as one principal family for the source’s central covenant-proximity question, retaining all three TEM proxies, all three AEM proxies, and all four REM outcomes. The introduction states the relation is examined across AEM, REM, and TEM; Table 2 is the first main empirical test. Later SOX, financial-distress, analyst-forecast, governance, and debt-feature analyses are separate follow-up questions and are excluded.

The modified-Jones construction has a source scaling inconsistency: Eq. (1) fits TAC_q/A_(q−1), but Eq. (2) prints TAC_q without that denominator before subtracting the fitted scaled terms. The formula is recorded as printed and the mismatch is flagged for AEMDA and downstream measures.
The source defines quantile regression for Table 2 but does not report the fitted quantile. Eqs. (4)–(6) are residual-generating fits whose estimator is not named; no OLS assumption is added.
Eq. (6) and its accompanying prose conflict over the CFO denominator. This affects REMCFO and every retained variable using REMCOMBINE. Supporting-fit sample counts are not reported.
results_review_notes: All 10 selected Table 2 baseline fits, their 117 frozen predictors, intercepts, coefficient estimates and direct p-values, fit-level Wald/LR rows, and fit observation counts are retained. Table 2 does not report coefficient standard errors or identify the fitted quantile.
Table 2 note says financial variables are winsorized at the 1st and 99th percentiles; this applies to the regression models. Firm and quarter-year indicators are YES, with no coefficients reported.

Table 1 descriptives are retained for 14 matched baseline outcomes and related current-ratio, market-to-book, CFO and assets measures. It reports no values for the other retained controls; non-retained leverage, ROA and debt-size rows are excluded.

Table 1 reports Mean, Q1, Median, and Q3 by CLOSE/DEFAULT/FAR group (Obs.=1,655/2,927/10,234). Those are group Ns, not variable-specific Ns, and the descriptive groups do not equal every complete-case Table 2 fit sample.
Table 2 prints ΔGDP and the clipped Panel B label REMCOMBIN; stable model-local terms are retained by named table row and column. The panel row maps to the specification variable REMCOMBINE.

The paper describes REMCOMBINE as REMPROD minus REMEXP minus REMCFO after reversing the signs of the latter components (p. 11), while Table 6 calls it the sum of the three components (p. 30). Both source statements are preserved.
